title: How Figma Uses AI Agents for Security
gist: Figma's security engineering team built AI agents on Panther SIEM that triage alerts using models like Claude Opus, cutting complex-alert resolution time by about 70% and on-call pages by 20%, while a companion vulnerability-finding agent caught more than 100 previously unknown bugs and reached 80% code-review precision within a month.

insights.claim: Figma's engineering team built AI agents that investigate security alerts, search past incidents, check company systems across cloud providers, and prepare code fixes, while keeping human review and strict controls in place.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Figma offers a production-grade template for AI-augmented security operations that other SaaS companies with mature SIEM stacks could replicate.
insights.locator: opening paragraph describing Figma's security agents

insights.claim: Figma's AI security agents helped engineers resolve complex alerts about 70% faster by learning from previous investigations and reducing repetitive work.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: A 70% reduction in alert-resolution time is a concrete productivity benchmark investors can use to test AI-agent ROI claims in security operations.

insights.claim: Figma's security system is built on Panther SIEM and investigates alerts and audit logs across AWS, Okta, GitHub, GCP, and osquery, querying more than 100 other sources and opening pull requests directly.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: The breadth of integrated data sources (100+) shows the scale of plumbing required before an AI agent becomes useful for real security triage, a barrier to entry for smaller competitors.
insights.locator: paragraph describing the Panther SIEM system

insights.claim: Figma's approach reduced resolution time by about 70% for complex alerts and cut on-call pages by 20% by automatically lowering the severity of some alerts.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Reduced on-call burden is a direct operational-cost saving investors can factor into engineering headcount efficiency models for AI-augmented security teams.

insights.claim: Figma's alert triage agent, which uses a model like Claude Opus, receives the full Slack thread history as context, its own steering memory, and a toolset scoped to what a human on-call security engineer typically needs during triage.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Figma's explicit use of Claude Opus for triage is a data point on which frontier model enterprises trust for high-stakes security workflows.
insights.quote: The alert triage agent (using a model like Claude Opus) is where most of the investigation happens. It receives the full Slack thread history as context, its own steering memory (more on this later), and a set of tools scoped to what a security on-call engineer typically needs during triage.
insights.locator: quote from Matthew Sullivan and Brad Girardeau

insights.claim: Figma's agentic system draws on AWS Bedrock Knowledge Bases, Amazon Kendra, Tines, and a Snowflake-based tool to search historical alerts and investigate data from Panther.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: The named vendor stack (Bedrock, Kendra, Tines, Snowflake) signals which infrastructure providers are capturing enterprise AI-security workloads.
insights.locator: paragraph naming AWS Bedrock Knowledge Bases

insights.claim: Figma's security engineers found that memory had the most impact on the system's usefulness over time, and keeping separate types of memory distinct was important to that success.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Memory design, not raw model capability, is emerging as the key differentiator for durable enterprise AI-agent value, a pattern applicable well beyond security.
insights.quote: Memory ended up being the thing that had the most impact on how useful the system became over time. We have several kinds, and keeping them separate turned out to be important.

insights.claim: Figma's system uses three distinct types of memory, past alerts, behavioral guidance, and learned database structures, to improve investigations over time.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: A taxonomy of memory types offers a reusable design pattern for enterprises building agentic workflows on internal, evolving data.

insights.claim: Figma built safety controls directly into its agent tools, setting agent-created pull requests to draft by default and designing prompts to prevent sensitive data from being shared in public Slack channels.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Defaulting agent output to a draft/review-required state is a low-cost guardrail pattern that limits the blast radius of AI-agent mistakes in production code and data workflows.
insights.locator: paragraph on safety controls built into tools

insights.claim: In a related effort described in 'How Figma stays ahead of vulnerabilities with agents,' Figma's agents found more than 100 previously unknown vulnerabilities, including two critical flaws that traditional tools had missed.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Discovering critical flaws that traditional static-analysis tools missed is direct evidence that agentic review can outperform legacy tooling on precision, not just speed.
insights.locator: paragraph on 'How Figma stays ahead of vulnerabilities'

insights.claim: Figma's AI code reviewer reached 80% precision within a month, improved detection of known bugs by about 30% through a second review step, and reduced some coding errors by about 50% after adding automated guidance.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: These precision and error-reduction figures give investors a concrete benchmark set for evaluating AI code-review vendors' marketing claims.
insights.locator: same paragraph, code reviewer precision metrics

insights.claim: Figma's security engineers argue teams building AI review agents should improve precision before recall, since existing historical bugs can only measure recall and do little to help fix the precision problems that must be addressed first.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: This counterintuitive sequencing, precision before recall, is a transferable engineering lesson for any team building AI-driven detection systems, security or otherwise.
insights.quote: We can't tell you exactly what to do: The specifics depend on your company size, the risks you face, and the feedback loops you already run. But one main lesson is to improve precision before recall. The order is counterintuitive, because the historical bugs you already have can only measure recall; they barely help with the precision you must fix first.

insights.claim: Cloud security company Wiz reported in 'GhostApproval: A Trust Boundary Gap in AI Coding Assistants' that six AI coding assistants could be tricked by malicious repositories into showing users a harmless-looking approval prompt.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: A named vulnerability class affecting six AI coding assistants is a concrete security risk investors should track when assessing exposure of AI-coding-tool vendors and their enterprise customers.

insights.claim: Figma concludes that as AI agents take on more security responsibility, the right balance between automation and human oversight is still evolving, framing the issue as complementary rather than a binary choice between AI and humans.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Enterprises should expect the human-in-the-loop requirement for AI security agents to persist rather than disappear, shaping compliance and staffing expectations even as automation scales.
insights.locator: final paragraph on balance between automation and oversight
